citations.text: Barzilai, S., & Chinn, C. A. (2024). The AIR and Apt-AIR frameworks of epistemic performance and growth: Reflections on educational theory development. Educational Psychology Review, 36(3), 91.

en.general: An individual or group method for reaching an epistemic aim that has a good chance of success, given the standards being used. Examples are running a fair experiment, weighing evidence by its quality, checking a claim against other sources, and arguing a question out in a group.

examples: Relating each piece of evidence to each competing model before choosing one.
A group critique in which different views are heard and objections are taken up.
nonExamples: Choosing the answer that feels right without checking, which can occasionally succeed but has no reason to be expected to.
